prompt:
You are working on a real infrastructure design problem for the grok-build agent harness (a Rust, OpenAI-Codex-style agent harness that runs OpenAI "codex family" models (gpt-5.6-sol/terra/luna), Anthropic models (claude-opus/sonnet), and others through an OpenAI-protocol-compatible proxy).

CAMPAIGN GOAL: make first-party OpenAI models on this custom harness as cheap and efficient as they are on the official OpenAI Codex CLI. The core cost problem is "upstream churn": redundant token traffic to the model API — cache invalidation, cache re-writes, wasted turns, duplicated or reordered context.

EVIDENCE BASE (wire-verified; cite these as E1-E6 in your doc):
E1. A/B on identical task, official codex vs this harness, gpt-5.6-sol medium: codex $0.1788 / 6 LLM requests; harness $0.5027 / 16 requests (2.81x). Turn granularity (fewer, larger turns) is the dominant swing factor, not per-token price.
E2. A mid-prefix item-ordering bug on the harness responses wire: a "developer" item and <system-reminder> user items permanently swap relative order once mid-session, pinning the cached prefix (~10.3k tokens stuck; ~113-1,004 cache-write tokens/turn after the swap until the next cold write).
E3. The harness drops cache_write_tokens from its own usage bookkeeping: the wire carries input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens but the session usage.json records cacheCreationTokens 0 — a cost-observability gap.
E4. The harness exposes 29-31 built-in tools to first-party codex-family models; lazy MCP tool discovery adds ~2 turns per discovered tool.
E5. parallel_tool_calls: official codex sends explicit false; the harness omits it (API default true). The harness model parallelizes (5 function_calls in one turn observed) yet still takes 2.9x the turns.
E6. claude models on the messages wire: a single reasoning item exceeding the harness's local 10,000-token per-item cap makes the next turn's local validation fail (non-retryable) — the session bricks after a high-reasoning turn.
